claims.text: The untreated eutectic high-entropy alloy has coarse dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The untreated alloy has limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittle failure.
Dislocation pile-ups at internal phase boundaries cause localized stress concentrations, microcracking, and brittle failure in the untreated alloy.
Tailored thermomechanical processing can produce an ultrafine-grained duplex eutectic high-entropy alloy while retaining its lamellar character.
The appropriate treatment specifically consists of moderate cold rolling followed immediately by rapid annealing.
The proposed treatment will refine and homogenize the dual-phase lamellae.
The proposed treatment will form hierarchically organized nanotwins at or near the original internal boundaries.
Lamellar and grain refinement together with nanotwins will distribute dislocation motion more uniformly.
The refined, nanotwinned structure will reduce dislocation pile-ups at phase boundaries.
Reducing dislocation pile-ups will lower local stress concentrations.
The processed microstructure will suppress microcrack initiation during deformation.
The treatment will increase room-temperature tensile elongation relative to the untreated alloy.
The treatment will maintain or increase room-temperature tensile yield strength and ultimate tensile strength relative to the untreated alloy.
Avoiding complete recrystallization while promoting fine grains and twins is necessary for the intended response.
Overly aggressive annealing can cause structural overgrowth or loss of the beneficial lamellar twin structure.
Loss of the lamellar twin structure would reduce the proposed dislocation-blunting effect.
The deformation strain and annealing temperature and duration must be calibrated to balance ultrafine structure formation against over-recrystallization and loss of phase stability.
